start: Take position `i` out and look at what is left: everything before it and everything after it, two pieces that do not touch. For `[2, 3, 4]` at index 1 that is `2` on the left and `4` on the right. When one side is empty, what should it contribute so the other side comes through unchanged?

Two passes. Going forward, carry `prefix`, the product of everything strictly before `i`: write it into the answer at `i`, then multiply `prefix` by `nums[i]`. Going backward, carry `suffix` the same way and multiply it into the answer. Both start at `1`, the product of nothing, and neither may include `nums[i]` when it is used at `i`.

start.text: The shape, with the two passes left to you:

test_boundaries: `[]` gives `[]`, `[7]` gives `[1]`, `[0, 3, 4]` gives `[12, 0, 0]` and `[0, 0, 4]` gives `[0, 0, 0]`. `[2, 3, 4]` gives `[12, 8, 6]`, and the list passed in must still be `[2, 3, 4]` afterwards. `[False]` must raise `ValueError`: `False` passes `isinstance(x, int)`, so compare `type(x) is int`.

`[7]` for `[7]` means a running product took `nums[i]` before it was stored at `i`: store first, then multiply. Dividing the total by `nums[i]` fails on `[0, 3, 4]`, which is why the rules forbid division. If the input changed, you wrote the answers into `nums` itself.
test_independent_exclusion_oracle: Every tuple of up to 5 values from `-2` to `2`, 3,906 of them, against `math.prod` of the tuple with position `i` left out. The first call passes the empty tuple `()` and expects `[]`: the answer must always be a new `list`, even when `nums` is a tuple.

`()` where `[]` was expected means the answer was built from `nums` itself, with `nums[:]` or `type(nums)(...)`: a slice of a tuple is a tuple. A `ValueError` on valid input means your type check accepts only lists; the contract allows tuples too.

ZeroDivisionError: Dividing the product of everything by `nums[i]` fails as soon as a value is `0`, as in `[0, 3, 4]`. No division is needed: the answer at `i` is the product of the values before `i` times the product of the values after it.
IndexError: The backward pass runs from `len(nums) - 1` down to `0`. `range(len(nums), -1, -1)` starts one past the end, which fails even on `[]`; `reversed(range(len(nums)))` gives exactly the right indices.
AttributeError: `'tuple' object has no attribute 'copy'`: `test_independent_exclusion_oracle` passes tuples, and a tuple has no `.copy()`. Build the answer as a new list of the right length, which works for both.

stopped: A backward `while i >= 0:` loop needs `i -= 1` on every turn; without it the loop multiplies into the same entry forever. `for i in reversed(range(len(nums))):` cannot forget the step.
If the run stopped for output, any `print` inside either pass is enough: `test_independent_exclusion_oracle` makes 3,906 calls. Print only for your own input, or use a breakpoint.
passing: All passing. As your own input, try `product_except_self([1, -1] * 10000)` and look at the memory: about 160 KB, the 20,000-entry answer list alone, which is the constant extra space the brief asked for. Separate prefix and suffix lists would roughly triple it. Then the README's follow-up: the same answers modulo a number.
